chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari, and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father Abdullah, from Ali ibn Isma'il Al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Amr Al-Zayyat, from Qa'id [Fayd] Al-Hannat, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically in the context of Ziyarah pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Al-Husayn with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Kazim (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the efficacy of Ziyarah lies not merely in physical presence but in 'Irfan'—a deep, cognizant recognition of Imam Al-Husayn’s (peace be upon him) spiritual station and rights. In Shia tradition, this specific acknowledgment transforms the visit into a means of comprehensive absolution, covering both past transgressions and future sins, thereby linking the commemoration of Karbala directly to individual soteriology.
